title: Zest will book a table from a text, if you have linked a card
friendlyTitle: Zest can book a restaurant from a text, if you link a card
summary: On 30 October Zest opened a restaurant concierge you reach by text, including in a group chat. It can blend tastes, run a vote, and book through OpenTable, Resy, or SevenRooms. The suggestions start from where people have actually eaten. Zest imports food and drink transactions through Plaid, the same link many banks use, rather than asking for a long preference interview. TechCrunch said its own tests returned usable options for time, party size, and place.
friendlySummary: On 30 October Zest opened a restaurant helper you reach by text, including in a group chat. It can mix people's tastes, run a vote, and book a table through OpenTable, Resy, or SevenRooms. The suggestions start from where people have actually eaten. Zest reads food and drink purchases through Plaid, a service many banks already use, instead of asking a long list of questions. TechCrunch said its own tests returned usable options for time, group size, and place.
whyItMatters: The booking is the useful part. The data trade is the part to decide first. Linking a card gives Zest a map of meals, limited to food and drink categories, and that history is what the text agent uses. Zest says booking is its first revenue line. If you do not want a startup reading card transactions, the text number is not a free concierge. It is the same product, reached from messages instead of the app.
